claim: BLI-4 and the collagen N-terminal furin site are required for SQT-3 and DPY-17 processing
finding: In bli-4 and cleavage-site mutants SQT-3 and DPY-17 are not efficiently secreted and form large intracellular aggregates; cuticle assembly reduced not blocked
context: C. elegans embryo, hypodermis, live imaging of endogenous SQT-3::mNG and DPY-17::mNG
confidence: high for requirement; does not demonstrate direct cleavage biochemically

claim: The consensus furin cleavage sites of DPY-17 and SQT-3 are functionally required
finding: CFCS sites of DPY-17 and SQT-3 required for Q neuroblast left-right migration; bli-4 mutants show only weak effects, attributed to isoform redundancy
context: C. elegans, Q neuroblast migration assay
confidence: moderate; weak bli-4 phenotype weakens the enzyme-substrate link in this assay

claim: A cuticle procollagen R-X-X-R site is a functional convertase site acting with bli-4
finding: All dpy-5 alleles dominantly suppress bli-4 blistering; mutating the DPY-5 RXXR causes dominant Dumpy
context: C. elegans hypodermis, dpy-5::gfp and allele analysis
confidence: moderate-high for DPY-5; BLI-4 named as candidate, not proven enzyme

finding: h384 molecular null replaces catalytically essential Ser415 with Phe; lethal mutations cluster in the protease domain

claim: bli-4 encodes kex2/subtilisin-family convertases with four C-terminally distinct isoforms
finding: Blisterases A-D share an N terminus; e937 deletes exon 13 unique to blisterase A and gives viable adult cuticle blistering
context: C. elegans, cDNA and genomic cloning
confidence: high; isoform complexity is a confound for substrate assignment

finding: DPY-31 astacin is responsible for C-terminal processing of SQT-3; nine dominant suppressors alter the SQT-3 C terminus
confidence: high; concerns the C terminus, not the N-terminal BLI-4 site

claim: Is a bli-4 effect on SQT-3 necessarily direct
finding: DPY-17 and SQT-3 extracellular assemblies are interdependent; loss of DPY-17 causes extensive intracellular retention of SQT-3
confidence: high; provides an explicit indirect route for the SQT-3 phenotype

claim: BLI-4 has furin-type specificity determinants and the collagen sites are conserved and accessible
finding: 12/12 furin catalytic+S1/S4 residues conserved in BLI-4; N-terminal R-X-X-R in 15/16 collagens at 5.5x over shuffled null, median 26 aa upstream of Gly-X-Y, site pLDDT 49.1 vs 58.0 protein mean (p=0.019); 93% conserved across 10 Caenorhabditis species
context: UniProt, AlphaFold DB v6, in silico
confidence: moderate; prediction only, and cannot discriminate BLI-4 from paralogues

claim: Can sequence analysis assign these sites to BLI-4 specifically
finding: All four C. elegans PCSKs (BLI-4, KPC-1, EGL-3, AEX-5) retain 11-12/12 furin pocket residues; KPC-1 is more furin-like than BLI-4 (57.5% vs 46.5% identity to furin)
confidence: high; motif analysis alone cannot assign the substrate to BLI-4

claim: Paralogue tissue partitioning supplies the specificity that sequence cannot
finding: KPC-1 broadly expressed in neurons and epithelia; AEX-5 functions in the intestine; EGL-3 required in cholinergic motor neurons for neuropeptide processing
confidence: moderate; KPC-1 epithelial expression leaves possible overlap with hypodermis
